claim.why_it_matters: Every prose line of 3.4 carries the ║ level-2 marker, but the general format block carries none, unlike the DISABLE and ENABLE formats (pages 676, 678) whose pre blocks are framed with ╔ ║ ╚ markers; read alone, the format looks like a level-1 element although the PURGE statement is level 2 only.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 680 shows a single rectangular box from the 3.4 heading through general rule (3); the line 'PURGE cd-name-1' (PURGE underlined) under 3.4.2 lies inside that box, so it is level-2 material. In page-680.md every heading and rule paragraph is wrapped in ║...║, but the <pre> block holding the general format carries no level-2 marker at all. The transcription's own convention for a boxed format (page 676, DISABLE, specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md lines 25331-25337) frames the pre block with ╔ ║ ╚ ... ╗ ║ ╝. The format text itself (PURGE underlined, cd-name-1) is transcribed correctly; what is missing is the level-2 marking of the format, which is content in this edition's notation (the box designates level-2 elements). The claim quotes both sources accurately.
